title: Runway Controller: SLO-failure anticipator for staged rollbacks
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Problem: Current canary rollback rules react to instantaneous SLO breaches (e.g., 95th latency spike, token-cost runups, or error rate jumps) and often trigger noisy or premature evictions. We lack a unified mechanism that: 1) anticipates an impending SLO breach using short-term trend forecasts across latency, error rate, token cost, and throughput; 2) normalizes heterogeneous signals into a single runway budget metric per cohort; and 3) enacts staged, proportional rollbacks (graceful degradation) using hysteresis and cohort prioritization to avoid unnecessary full evictions.

Goal: Implement a "Runway Controller" that computes a runway budget per canary cohort representing time (or tokens) until modeled SLO exhaustion, and use that budget to drive automated staged rollback policies with tunable hysteresis. The controller should: (a) fuse latency, errors, token burn-rate, and throughput into a single failure-anticipation score using EWMA + short-term AR(1) prediction; (b) convert score into runway expressed in minutes and token-units; (c) apply exponential hysteresis per cohort to prevent oscillation; (d) provide config knobs for cost-first vs latency-first rollback preferences; and (e) expose explainability traces for audit/debug.

Why this is valuable: Predictive rollback reduces unnecessary flapping, preserves user experience by preferring capacity throttles and partial traffic reallocation, and lowers incident toil. It also lets product teams balance cost vs latency by selecting pre-made profiles (cost-aware, latency-conservative, balanced).

Scope: Controller logic in runtime-orchestration service, config UI in Console (limited knobs), evaluation harness for offline simulation, and end-to-end e2e tests in staging. Minimal changes to the serving runtime: telemetry hooks and an opt-in control plane API to evict cohorts at fractional traffic percentages.

Out of scope: Full ML-based anomaly detector (we keep lightweight forecasting using EWMA/AR(1) initially); private deployment UX changes (will follow after hosted validation).
acceptance_criteria: Controller computes runway budget for each active cohort every 30s and stores last 6 windows in traces
For synthetic canaries (benchmark suite), controller avoids >50% unnecessary full-evictions compared to baseline heuristic rules over 48h replay
Config profiles (cost-aware, latency-conservative, balanced) available in Console and accepted by rollout API
Controller supports staged rollback: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with hysteresis timers between steps
Explainability trace includes contributing signals and short-term forecast used for each decision
New alerts generated when runway < 2 minutes and escalation playbook link included
Unit and integration tests cover forecasting, fusion, and hysteresis transitions with deterministic seeds
design_notes: Signal fusion: normalize signals to z-scores using rolling baseline per cohort (30m window). Compute weighted sum where weights are tunable per profile. Default weights: latency_p95=0.4, errors=0.3, token_burn_rate=0.2, throughput_drop=0.1.

Forecasting: EWMA for short smoothing (alpha=0.3) plus AR(1) on last 3 samples to project 1-minute and 5-minute horizons. Use projection to estimate time-to-SLO-exceedance under steady-state sampling rate.
Runway metric: convert projected exceedance into runway minutes and token-budget (tokens left before cost budget breach). Use min(minutes, token_minutes) as conservative runway value.
Hysteresis: exponential backoff on rollback reversal (e.g., once stepped down from 30% -> 10% revert requires runway > baseline_for_recover * 1.5 for at least 3 consecutive windows).
Cohort prioritization: cohorts with highest customer_impact tag are throttled last; internal experiments default to lowest CX impact cohorts first.
API: control-plane endpoint /v1/rollouts/{id}/actions accepts fractional_traffic adjustments and reason payload with trace_id. Runtime honors fractional adjustments if opt-in flag enabled.
Explainability: store last 6 forecasts + signal contributions in traces (max 6KB per trace) and surface minimal summary in Console to satisfy audits.
Safety: daily dry-run mode where controller runs but only logs decisions (no enforcement) for the first week in production before enabling enforcement for new rollout IDs.
rollout_plan: Week 0 (staging): deploy controller in dry-run mode for internal canaries. Validate traces and forecast quality using replay dataset (production sample).
Week 1 (beta): enable enforcement for <5% of traffic for test customers. Use manual guardrails: require ops approval for full rollout escalations.
Week 2 (gradual): open enforcement to all staged rollouts but with conservative profile default; monitor false positives/negatives for 7 days.
Post-deploy (4w): evaluate metrics, iterate weights and hysteresis params, prepare Console docs and runbook updates.
monitoring_and_alerts: Runway < 5m alert (P2) -> Slack #ops-rollouts with trace link
Runway < 2m alert (P1) -> On-call + runbook with immediate mitigation steps
Controller decision rate spike (>3x baseline) -> investigate oscillation/hysteresis misconfig
Daily summary dashboard: % of canaries where controller intervened, median runway at intervention, rollback stage distribution
Post-action evaluation: automated replay job re-simulates decision and reports expected vs observed user impact
